items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: Fletcher Henderson was one of the first colored men to copy from the records of the Dixieland Jazz Band.

ctx.x: Well, Paul Whiteman, Kid Tua Jazz. Mamie Smith and her jazz hands. I have them records of all of them. Clarence Williams' Blue Five and the Clarence Williams' Blue Rhythm Band, which was featuring Louis Armstrong, Donald Redmond, that's spelled R-E-D-M-O-N-D, Busta Bailey, Coleman Hawkins, etc. Louis Armstrong's first record that brought him recognition was Everybody Loves My Baby, which he recorded with the Clarence Williams' Blue Five. Fletcher Henderson and Benny Morton of Kansas City were also...
They were imitators of the Dixieland Jazz Band. Fletcher Henderson was one of the first colored men to copy from the records of the Dixieland Jazz Band.
Fletcher Henderson and Benny Morton of Kansas City were also among the first swing artists. Benny Morton's name is spelled M-O-R-T-O-N. Do you want me to read the letter to the editor? Just a moment.
